mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of quarters where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 8% triggers a recessionary demand shock that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that erode corporate earnings expectations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods matching the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) accompanied by a concurrent rise in the consumer price index above 3% indicates a supply-side shock that raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day forward returns in more than 55% of episodes meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods matching the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1% combined with a year-over-year decline in CPI below 1% indicates an extended period of monetary accommodation that supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 fails to deliver positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons for three consecutive months signals weak labor demand that depresses corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods matching the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 2% with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 7% signals a broad-based demand contraction that reliably produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of episodes meeting the trigger.
